fixes.explanation: Not quite, baker, and the text is blunt about it. The announcement says Bel is put to shame, Marduk is shattered, her images are disgraced and her idols are broken in pieces (Jeremiah 50:2). Bel and Marduk are Babylon's false gods. Her idols are broken in pieces, so they don't come through in one piece.

Right, the idols don't come through in one piece. The announcement says Bel is put to shame and Marduk is shattered. Her images are disgraced, and her idols are broken in pieces (Jeremiah 50:2). Bel and Marduk are Babylon's false gods. I've dropped a tray of cookies, and even that's a gentler landing.

No prize to split here, baker. The verse says the nation from the north will make her land a desolation. No one will live in it, and both man and beast will flee (Jeremiah 50:3). That's a desolation, not a prize for two kings.

Yes, both of them. The LORD says the children of Israel and the children of Judah will come together, weeping as they come, and will seek the LORD their God (Jeremiah 50:4). Two groups, one direction. Tissues for everybody.
Resting place, yes. The LORD says they've wandered from mountain to hill and “…have forgotten their resting place.” (Jeremiah 50:6). Somebody get these folks a chair.
Hiding isn't the word the LORD uses, friend. He says they “…have forgotten their resting place.” (Jeremiah 50:6). The verse says they roam the mountains and wander from mountain to hill.
No meeting here, baker, and no calendar invite either. The verse says they have wandered from mountain to hill and “…have forgotten their resting place.” (Jeremiah 50:6). The word is resting.

That's their speech. Their enemies said, “We are not guilty, for they have sinned against the LORD, their true pasture, the LORD, the hope of their fathers.” (Jeremiah 50:7). It's a tidy excuse, and it names the LORD twice.

This one is true, friend. The LORD says, “For behold, I stir up and bring against Babylon an assembly of great nations from the land of the north.” (Jeremiah 50:9). The call to leave comes right before that.

Least, yes. The LORD says the plunderers' mother will be greatly ashamed, and “Behold, she will be the least of the nations, a wilderness, a dry land, and a desert.” (Jeremiah 50:12). That's a long fall from the loud celebration just before it.

Right, they don't admire her. Because of the wrath of the LORD, she will not be inhabited and will become completely desolate. “All who pass through Babylon will be horrified and will hiss at all her wounds.” (Jeremiah 50:13). Horrified and hissing is the opposite of admiring.

The LORD doesn't leave the archers guessing, baker. He says, “Shoot at her! Spare no arrows! For she has sinned against the LORD.” (Jeremiah 50:14). Orders and reason come in the same breath, and the reason is the one you picked.

Hands up, baker. The LORD calls for a war cry against her on every side, and the text says, “She has thrown up her hands in surrender; her towers have fallen; her walls are torn down.” (Jeremiah 50:15). Surrender, fallen towers and torn-down walls all sit in the same verse.
No phone calls to allies in this verse, baker. It says, “She has thrown up her hands in surrender…” (Jeremiah 50:15). Her hands are up in surrender, not dialing anybody.

Same, yes, baker. The LORD says, “Since this is the vengeance of the LORD, take out your vengeance upon her; as she has done, do the same to her.” (Jeremiah 50:15). The measure is what she has done. Same deed, same treatment.

Satisfied, yes. The LORD says, “I will return Israel to his pasture, and he will graze on Carmel and Bashan; his soul will be satisfied on the hills of Ephraim and Gilead.” (Jeremiah 50:19). Grazing on Carmel and Bashan comes right before it. Think of the feeling when you finally sit down after a long shift on your feet, only bigger.

None, baker. The LORD says, “…a search will be made for Israel’s guilt, but there will be none…” (Jeremiah 50:20). Somebody goes looking and comes back empty-handed, which is the best kind of empty. The same verse says, “…for I will forgive the remnant I preserve.” (Jeremiah 50:20).
